newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares shuffle sideways, SIA slumps.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares shuffle sideways, SIA slumps.

text.p: Singapore shares opened almost unchanged on Tuesday with brokers predicting the local index could slip a little later as investors continued to take profits after the run-up last week.

Singapore Airlines' (SIA) foreign shares fell three percent, or 40 cents to Singapore $12.60, as brokers executed sell-orders put in place overnight by overseas investors following news of the carrier's disappointing half-year results.
By 0145 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 0.40 points lower at 2,067.45. Volume was a modest 7.9 million shares with 44 losers and 17 gainers.
SIA's foreign shares topped the actives list with 1.3 million shares traded. Dealers said part of the selling was due to broker downgrades.
SIA's local share tranche was down five cents at S$7.50.

Malaysia's Faber Group was the biggest gainer in the early morning, rising six percent, or eight cents to S$1.44, after it was among a group of three companies awarded a 15-year hospital support contract by the Malaysian government.
